fixes.title: "Best night" star lands on the worst night of the week when the project has no targets
fixes.summary: WeekForecast.bestNight (night_forecast.dart:205) only advanced on a strict `>`, so when every night tied it kept the EARLIEST. NightForecast.score is 0 for any night with no darkness, no clear dark time, or no project target up, so an empty project made all seven nights tie at 0 and night one was starred (and rendered with the selected-card accent) no matter how clouded it was - 0.0/6.2h clear starred while 5.0/6.4h clear sat next to it unmarked. bestNight now returns null when the maximum score is 0: there is no best night when nothing is imageable on any of them. WeekForecastStrip already renders correctly for a null best (isBest false everywhere), so no widget change was needed.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/week_forecast_strip_test.dart -> 'no project target up: nothing is starred, not the earliest clouded night' (renders the real WeekForecastStrip over a two-night week with no targets, the earliest being the fully clouded one, and asserts no LucideIcons.star and no SkotiqCard with isSelected). Plus the polar-night expectation in packages/skotiq_core/test/services/planning/forecast_planning_service_test.dart was flipped to isNull.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the single production line `if (best != null && best.score <= 0.0) return null;` from night_forecast.dart bestNight. week_forecast_strip_test.dart: 7 pass, 1 fail ('no project target up: ...'). Restored -> 8/8 pass, and core forecast_planning_service_test + night_forecast_test 32/32 pass.
fixes.caveats: Behaviour change visible elsewhere: a polar-summer week (0 dark hours) now also reports no best night, which is why the existing polar test's expectation was inverted. That is the honest answer for a night with no darkness at all.

fixes.title: Sunrise and sunset are 3.5-4 minutes wrong (atmospheric refraction counted twice)
fixes.summary: Every crossing search in astronomy_calculations.dart evaluates APPARENT altitude (sunAltitude and _apparentAltitudeOf both add Saemundsson refraction), but the rise/set targets _sunRiseSetAltitude = -0.8333 and _moonRiseSetAltitude = -0.7 are GEOMETRIC sun/moon-centre altitudes whose -34' term IS the refraction allowance. Comparing them directly spent refraction twice: sunset came out ~3.5 min late and sunrise ~4.4 min early (7.5 min of daylight invented per day), while the twilight angles were unharmed because atmosphericRefraction is suppressed below -2 deg. Added AstronomyCalculations._apparentLimb(geometric) = trueToApparentAltitude(geometric) and routed all four rise/set call sites through it (calculateTwilightTimes sunset + sunrise, calculateSunVisibility, calculateMoonVisibility). Refraction is monotonic in altitude there, so crossing apparent == _apparentLimb(x) is exactly crossing geometric == x - the USNO/NOAA convention.
fixes.test: NEW packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/sunrise_sunset_refraction_test.dart - pins calculateTwilightTimes for the reported site (40.0N/-75.0W, 2026-08-01) against an INDEPENDENT NOAA solar-position solve (scratchpad/sunsolve.py, 30 s grid + 50-step bisection, geometric -0.8333): sunset 2026-08-02T00:13:37Z, sunrise 2026-08-02T09:59:24Z, astro dusk 02:01:44Z, astro dawn 08:11:16Z, each to under 2 minutes, plus the convention invariant (geometric sun altitude at the returned sunset/sunrise IS -0.8333) for both the twilight path and calculateSunVisibility, and the -0.7 moon limb. Two existing tests in rise_set_transit_test.dart asserted the WRONG convention (apparent altitude at the -0.833 limb) and were corrected to the geometric altitude; twilight_window_test.dart's brute-force oracle scanned apparent altitude against the geometric target and was corrected the same way (it would otherwise agree with the bug).
fixes.revert_check: Replaced the body of _apparentLimb with `geometricAltDeg` (identity = old behaviour), leaving all four call sites wired. 22 failures: 4 in sunrise_sunset_refraction_test.dart, 2 in rise_set_transit_test.dart, and 16 of the 18 site/date cases in twilight_window_test.dart (errors of 3-22 minutes, largest at high latitude where the sun grazes). Restored -> 88/88 pass across sunrise_sunset_refraction, rise_set_transit, twilight_window, night_in_progress_window, coordinate_system and mosaic_planner; the 35 app tests that read sunset/sunrise (night_timeline, command_bar, observing_site_gating, no_site_sentinel, altitude_chart_now_marker) stay green.
fixes.caveats: Moonrise/moonset move by a similar few minutes. The verifier called the moon half 'plausible' rather than reproduced; it is the identical mechanism on the same constant and is now covered by the -0.7 limb invariant.

fixes.title: Night Outlook hero card freezes its "Alt" and "Airmass" readouts
fixes.summary: LOCATION CORRECTED (as the verifier found): the stale readout is in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart, not _primary_target_card.dart / _recommendation_tab.dart, and the candidate-list card was never 'still updating' - it uses the same AltitudeChart and only looked live because scrolling recycles it through initState. AltitudeChart computed _currentAltitude/_currentAirmass exclusively inside _calculateData, called from initState and from didUpdateWidget on a ra/dec change; there was no timer and no clock provider in the widget, so chips labelled in the present tense stated whatever the sky looked like at mount, indefinitely. Added a 1-minute Timer.periodic in initState (cancelled in dispose) driving a new _refreshCurrentPosition() that re-solves only the now-quantities (one objectAltAz + airmass) and setStates - which also moves the red 'Now' marker, since its x is derived at build time. The night curve and twilight window are properties of the night, not the minute, so they are deliberately NOT re-solved per tick; but if the clock has left the plotted window entirely (app left open past dawn) the tick runs the full _calculateData instead.
fixes.test: NEW packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/framing/altitude_chart_live_readout_test.dart - mounts the real AltitudeChart mid-night with a movable nowOverride, records the rendered 'Alt: ' and 'Airmass: ' chip strings, advances the clock and the tester by 20 minutes WITHOUT rebuilding the parent, scrolling or changing ra/dec, and requires both chip strings to have changed. A second test tears the tree down and pumps 5 more minutes so a leaked timer fails the suite.
fixes.revert_check: Cut the production wiring only - the whole `_nowTicker = Timer.periodic(...)` statement in initState - leaving _refreshCurrentPosition and dispose intact. 'the Alt/Airmass readout tracks the clock, it does not freeze' failed; the dispose test still passed. Restored -> 6/6 pass across altitude_chart_live_readout_test and altitude_chart_now_marker_test.
fixes.caveats: 4 framing golden/capture tests (captures_landscape x2, framing_hips_layer_wiring, framing_registration) fail in this package - verified PRE-EXISTING by restoring altitude_chart.dart to its HEAD contents and re-running: identical 4 failures, 81% pixel diffs (Windows-captured goldens on Linux).

fixes.title: The minimum-altitude gate is 25 deg in the scheduler and 30 deg in the planner/sequence builder
fixes.summary: Two independent defaults for one physical quantity. Fixed both halves. (1) UNIFIED THE DEFAULT in the safe direction: SchedulerConfig.minAltitudeDegrees 25.0 -> 30.0, matching SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg, the targets.min_altitude column and the chart threshold. Raising the autopilot floor only makes it stricter - it can never now promise a target the builder refuses - whereas lowering the builder to 25 would have loosened a gate for every headless user who never opens the scheduler. (2) MADE IT ONE NUMBER: new siteMinimumAltitudeDegProvider in skotiq_core serves the operator's persisted scheduler minimum (the only editable one in the product, Plan Tonight > Schedule > Scoring weights) with SchedulerConfig.defaults as the pre-load answer; plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart now passes it as SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg (so the TargetHeader's min_altitude and its AltitudeAbove/Below triggers carry it), as the calculateObjectVisibility floor, and as the mosaic panel minAltitude; altitude_chart.dart draws its dashed threshold at it instead of a hard-coded 30 (the grid's separate 'value == 30' highlight is gone with it). scheduler_tab_content._applySchedulerConfig now invalidates schedulerPersistedConfigProvider after a successful local save so a slider move reaches those surfaces in the same session - safe because the engine takes that provider through ref.listen and skips while schedulerConfigUserDirtyProvider is set. Per-target targets.min_altitude overrides are untouched and still live (ForecastTarget.minAltitudeDeg, forecast_planning_service.dart:243); this provider is the site FLOOR, not a replacement.
fixes.test: THREE, one per production call site. (a) packages/skotiq_app/test/utils/plan_tonight_site_min_altitude_test.dart drives the real buildPlanTonightTargetSequenceFromSuggestion with the DURABLE scheduler row overridden to 42 deg and asserts the emitted TargetHeaderNode.minAltitude / AltitudeAboveTrigger / AltitudeBelowTrigger are all 42, plus a second test that with no row saved the header equals SchedulerConfig.defaults.minAltitudeDegrees. (b) altitude_chart_live_readout_test.dart 'the threshold line marks the SITE minimum, not a fixed 30 deg' pumps the real chart with the row at 45 and asserts the single dashed HorizontalLine sits at y=45. (c) packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/site_minimum_altitude_test.dart pins the anti-drift invariant SchedulerConfig.defaults.minAltitudeDegrees == const SmartNightSettings().minAltitudeDeg, the provider's read-through, and its pre-load fallback.
fixes.revert_check: Cut both wirings at once - removed `minAltitudeDeg: ref.read(siteMinimumAltitudeDegProvider),` from the SmartNightSettings construction in plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart and put `y: 30` back in altitude_chart.dart. 2 failures: 'the built sequence gates on the SITE minimum altitude' and 'the threshold line marks the SITE minimum, not a fixed 30 deg'. Separately restored the 25.0 default: 'scheduler and Smart Night agree on the default minimum altitude' failed. Restored all three -> 13 pass across plan_tonight_site_min_altitude, altitude_chart_live_readout, plan_tonight_sequencer_helper_no_filter_wheel and plan_tonight_sequencer_helper_mosaic; core scheduler suites 84 pass; site_minimum_altitude 3/3.
fixes.caveats: On a NetworkBackend the Schedule tab shows the HOST's config while the local builder reads the local durable row, so a host whose minimum was changed remotely can still differ. At defaults they now agree (30 vs 30) where before they could not (25 vs 30). Pre-existing, verified at HEAD by restoring altitude_chart.dart to its HEAD contents: 5 planner golden/capture tests fail on Linux (Windows-captured goldens).

fixes.title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is shared by every instance on the machine; the prompt cannot be dismissed
fixes.summary: TWO HALVES, DIFFERENT ANSWERS. (1) The path half was ALREADY FIXED in the working tree before I got here (not by me): app_shell.dart now has resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory(), which anchors the checkpoint on the directory holding the OPEN DATABASE plus a `checkpoints/` subfolder mirroring resolveHostCheckpointDirectory, with adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint() carrying a pre-6.1 support-dir file forward only when SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is unset. The finding's cited line (`final supportDir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory(); await backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path)`) no longer exists; the call site at app_shell.dart:438 passes resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory(). Covered by packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/checkpoint_directory_test.dart (4 tests, green). Left alone. (2) The dialog half: the verifier REFUTED the reporter's mechanism (a successful discard returns AppStartupCheckpointOutcome.discarded and exits the loop; only a THROWING resume/discard re-prompts) but the residual trap is real - runAppCheckpointRecovery loops forever on a throwing action, the modal is barrierDismissible:false with only Resume and Discard, so a backend that throws on both (read-only checkpoint dir, corrupt file) wedges the app behind the barrier. FIXED that: extracted the modal into a top-level visibleForTesting buildCheckpointRecoveryDialog and gave it a 'Not now' action that pops null (-> outcome failed, checkpoint left on disk). It appears ONLY once an attempt has failed, so a clean first run still has to be decided.
fixes.test: NEW packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/checkpoint_recovery_dialog_test.dart - shows the REAL dialog through showDialog(barrierDismissible: false) and asserts (a) no 'Not now' on the first prompt, (b) after a FileSystemException it renders 'Retry Resume' + the error and a working 'Not now' that closes the modal, (c) runAppCheckpointRecovery treats that null choice as stop-asking (2 prompts, outcome failed) instead of looping.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the `if (lastError != null) SkotiqButton(... 'Not now' ...)` action from buildCheckpointRecoveryDialog. 'after a failed attempt the operator can leave the modal' failed. Restored -> 3/3 pass, and the whole test/screens/shell suite is 77/77 green (including the pre-existing checkpoint_directory_test).
fixes.caveats: Outcome is 'partial' only because the larger half was already done by someone else this campaign - the path is verified correct, not merely assumed. The extraction moved _checkpointInfoRow from the State class to a top-level function; no behaviour change.
